newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Belo said denying controversial comments.
newsitem.headline: Belo said denying controversial comments.

text.p: Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo has denied telling a German journalist that Indonesia treated the people of East Timor like "scabby dogs", the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

"Belo, in a special consultation with local East Timor authorities, gave an explanation about what was quoted by the magazine and said it was not true," East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam was quoted as saying.
Muharam said Belo had signed a statement in which he denied ever telling the German magazine Der Spiegel that Indonesia treated East Timor's people like "scabby dogs".
Belo, who shared the Nobel Peace Prize last month with East Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, has declined to comment on the truth of the report until a news conference to be held next week.
The Beijing-based Der Spiegel correspondent said he stands by the details in the original story.
Belo was not immediately available for comment on Wednesday.
Youth groups aligned with the ruling Golkar party last week staged anti-Belo protests outside the parliament building in Jakarta and demanded the bishop retract his comments.

East Timorese then publicly rallied around Belo, a popular figure in the territory because of his strong stand on human rights, after the protests and further attacks by Indonesian government officials in the country's media.

Five days of demonstrations in support of the bishop climaxed on Saturday when witnesses said more than 60,000 people gathered to pray with Belo and listen to a speech at Dili's cathedral, in which he told them to stop protesting and go home.

Indonesia's control of East Timor still faces some political and armed resistance more than 20 years after Jakarta invaded in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following year.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's sovereignty over the former Portuguese colony, which it still regards as being administered by Lisbon.
